subject: Private deployment: on-prem VPC qualification + post-demo recap
messages:
Date: 2027-02-14T15:03:00-08:00
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lee <dana@fincorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Subject: Private deployment: on-prem VPC qualification + post-demo recap

Hi Dana — thanks again for your time on the demo earlier. Quick recap and a short checklist so we can align on whether Private VPC (VPC peering / PrivateLink) or Dedicated capacity is the right fit for FinCorp.

Key notes from our call:
- Primary requirement: customer data never leaves FinCorp network; must pass through customer-controlled VPC or on-prem gateway.
- Compliance: SOC2 + regional data residency; encryption at rest + KMS integration required.
- Expected throughput: sustained 100 rps, spikes to 400 rps during batch windows.
- Latency goal: p95 < 150ms for inference path.

Deployment options discussed (summary):
- Hosted API: fastest to launch but not acceptable due to data residency/traffic restriction.
- Dedicated: good for predictable throughput but still routes traffic via Redwood-managed egress; may be acceptable if we can setup PrivateLink.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full network isolation via VPC peering or PrivateLink; supports your control-plane constraints.

Network questions we need answers for to progress the Private VPC path:
1) Preferred connectivity: VPC peering (Amazon) vs PrivateLink vs on-prem Direct Connect / MPLS? If unsure, indicate priority: (a) minimal routing changes, (b) strict egress allowlist only, (c) fully on-prem NAT termination.
2) Egress IPs: please confirm static egress IPs or if you need a CIDR range. Redwood can provide stable outbound IPs for egress allowlist; we typically recommend a small /28 if peerable.
3) Firewall/ports: our runtime requires outbound TLS (443) and inbound management ports for healthchecks from Redwood control plane (we can proxy over 443). For peering mode, we need TCP 443 and ephemeral high ports for MTLS/kv sync — can work over 443 if required.
4) DNS: will you allow split-horizon DNS or do we need to support IP-based endpoints?
5) KMS/HSM integration: do you have a preferred KMS (AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault / on-prem HSM)?

Attached: redwood-onprem-deploy-checklist.pdf — lightweight checklist we use in preflight. Also included a sample allowlist CSV format (we'll populate after you confirm preferred connectivity).

Next steps we propose:
- Dana / NetOps: confirm preferred connectivity option and whether you can share a temporary test CIDR for the POC by EOD next Tue (2027-02-22).
- Redwood (Monica + Ben): will prepare a scoped network runbook and draft a limited-time allowlist for POC.
- Schedule a NetOps handoff call: suggest Wed 2/24 10:00 PT — CC'ing Monica and Ben to coordinate.

Thanks — look forward to the checklist answers so we can prepare the POC network config.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Date: 2027-02-15T09:12:00-08:00
From: Dana Lee <dana@fincorp.com>

Cc: FinCorp Network Team <netops@fincorp.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@consult-net.com>
Subject: Re: Private deployment: on-prem VPC qualification + post-demo recap

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap and checklist. A few clarifications from our side after an internal sync with NetOps and security: 

Answers to your numbered questions:
1) Connectivity: primary preference is PrivateLink (endpoint service) — minimal routing changes and preserves our egress controls. Secondary option is VPC peering if PrivateLink is not available for a specific region. We also have an on-prem Direct Connect circuit but prefer to avoid changes there for the POC.
2) Egress IPs: we need a fixed set of public IPs for allowlisting on our perimeter firewalls. For the POC we can accept a /29 (8 IPs). Please provide the exact IP list at least 3 business days before testing.
3) Firewall/ports: we can open outbound to Redwood IPs on 443. For management/healthcheck callbacks, prefer everything over 443 (no extra ephemeral ports). If there is a need for mutual TLS, we can accept that over 443 as well.
4) DNS: split-horizon is OK — we'll create a private hosted zone to resolve your private endpoint names.
5) KMS: we use AWS KMS for now; we would prefer Redwood to integrate with our KMS for key management if possible.

We'll attach our initial allowlist template and a short network diagram. Oliver from our consultant team will coordinate VPC endpoint setup if needed.

Timeline: we can aim for a POC window starting the week of 2/28 provided Redwood supplies the IP list and endpoint details by 2/24.

Thanks,
Dana
Director of Platform Engineering | FinCorp
dana@fincorp.com | +1 (212) 555-0987

Thanks Dana — this is helpful. Quick internal notes / ask from the infra side: 

Ben / Aditya — action items for us before 2/24: 
- Confirm whether we can publish a static /29 for POC egress (we can; I will coordinate with infra to reserve a contiguous block).
- Ensure control-plane callbacks are proxied over 443 only (confirm no ephemeral port requirement).
- KMS: we support AWS KMS cross-account decrypt via IAM role + re-encryption; we'll need FinCorp to create a cross-account key policy or provide an external key ARN. Monica to draft KMS onboarding steps.
- DNS: we'll provide a private endpoint hostname like pvt-api.us-west-2.redwood-inference.internal — need FinCorp to create a private hosted zone for that name.

Operational notes: 
- For PrivateLink we expose the inference endpoint as an NLB-backed service in our account and accept connections from your VPC endpoints. Benefits: no route table changes, only ENIs in your VPC; downside: extra setup for listeners and NLB cross-az.
- For VPC peering we need to confirm overlapping CIDR ranges (documented in the checklist). Peering is simpler for raw TCP but requires route updates.

I will attach a quick KMS onboarding doc (short bullet list) and a stubbed IP list once infra confirms. Ben — can you validate the /29 availability and whether we need to reserve an adjacent /28 in case of failover?

Monica
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
